### A01

Decision: P may be released now because its invocation permit was revoked before invocation. Q must retain its reservation despite cancellation until its evaluation settles and AGP disposes the retained work. R must retain its reservation until its owned result is disposed; settlement alone is insufficient. If disposal is performed at this checkpoint, R can then be released exactly once.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor.\"
QUOTE: \"On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A02

Decision: The old rejection cannot fault the replacement or release the replacement's reservation. Application checks the runtime gate, controller identity/incarnation, admission kind, exact token and deadline. The removed controller's completion is stale regardless of the shared peer identity or the replacement's timeliness. Its bounded accounting owner observes and disposes the old completion and releases only the old evaluation's reservation once settlement and disposal permit. It cannot introduce a new session fault or expiry.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Route the prepared completion through a short executor turn that checks the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, token and deadline;\"
QUOTE: \"Runtime authority revoked, controller replaced, admission kind/token stale, or another terminal cause already committed | Dispose the retained completion through its bounded owner; no admission event, identity effect, route effect or new terminal cause\"
QUOTE: \"Revocation detaches the result's session-effect target; a late observer retains only bounded work-accounting state, not a closure that keeps the controller and channel alive.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A03

Decision: Neither operation is permitted there. Normalize a potentially current provider result outside the executor into bounded, owned, immutable data, before serialized application. Property access, cloning or provider-controlled callbacks must not execute application code inside the executor. Abort-event delivery also belongs outside the executor, after serialized revocation/commit as appropriate. The serialized turn handles owned preparation, guards and installation; avoiding a handoff does not authorize application callbacks within that turn.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Normalize a potentially current provider result outside the executor into bounded owned immutable data; reject invalid shape without retaining an unbounded copy.\"
QUOTE: \"Property access, cloning and provider-controlled callbacks must not become application code running inside the executor.\"
QUOTE: \"Provider calls and abort-event delivery both stay outside the executor because either can run application code.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A04

Decision: Equality means expired. Discard the result-effect plan and its unconsumed ordinary permit. The session controller must prepare and preflight the route AdmissionExpired transition through the coordinator and commit it in this same serialized turn; it cannot return leaving progress dependent on timer delivery. With numeric room, route expiry invalidates the continuation, sends INTERNAL_ERROR only if safe, purges and releases. No result revision or ACK effect occurs. Work capacity still follows settlement-plus-disposal accounting.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Equality is expired, and provider settlement time does not replace the final application-time check.\"
QUOTE: \"A bound expires between preparation and the final guard | Discard the unconsumed ordinary permit and result plan; prepare and preflight the expiry transition in the same turn, with no result effects\"
QUOTE: \"The session controller owns the serialized transition; timer delivery and result application call the same expiry decision path, not separate terminal owners.\"
QUOTE: \"Route expiry retains the Established expiry actions: invalidate the continuation, send "'`INTERNAL_ERROR` only if safe, purge and release."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A05

Decision: In the first observation, OpenExpired wins because equal elapsed identity-admission and outer OPEN deadlines select the outer deadline. Delivery of the admission timer first cannot authorize AdmissionExpired instead. In the separate early-wake observation, neither expiry transition is authorized. Recheck monotonic time and rearm the admission timer only for its positive remainder; do not cancel the evaluation or terminate the session. The OPEN timer retains its own authority.

Document support:

QUOTE: "If both are elapsed, choose the earlier absolute deadline; equal deadlines choose the outer `OpenExpired` transition."
QUOTE: "While an identity evaluation is current, both admission/OPEN timer inputs and result-application guards use that same selection; callback arrival order cannot select the later bound."
QUOTE: "If neither bound has elapsed, a current timer input only rearms its own positive remainder; after identity commit, the still-active OPEN timer retains its separate authority through confirmation."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A06

Decision: On the scenario'"'s millisecond time scale, the absolute cleanup deadline is t=1000: terminal-cause commit at 100 plus 900 ms. At t=850, graceful close has only 150 ms of the total allowance remaining. It receives no fresh 900 ms, and the 2400 ms per-send setting cannot extend cleanup. This is proposed semantic migration of the existing close setting: adoption must update the FSM timer row, public descriptions and migration guidance together. Existing name, units, domain and default remain, but earlier teardown phases consume the allowance.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Start one absolute teardown deadline when the controller's terminal cause commits, using the resolved "'`timers.transportCloseTimeoutMs`."
QUOTE: "Its scope includes waiting for the terminal notification, any pending send, graceful close and observation of the sole reader'"'s terminal; later phases never receive a fresh budget.\"
QUOTE: \"The current FSM timer row instead starts transport-close timing at graceful-close start; adopting this revision must change that row and all public descriptions of the setting together.\"
QUOTE: \"Before adoption, inventory type/schema/config descriptions and callers that rely on close timing; record the changed interval in migration guidance.\"

### A07

Decision: Detachment preserves D or may force cleanup sooner; it cannot restart the deadline or disable its guard while terminal observation is pending. Numeric failure closes ordinary authority, but the transferred cleanup owner retains exact cleanup-generation authority and the original deadline. The later write timeout may force an earlier channel abort, but cannot replace the committed protocol cause, publish another teardown event or restart the budget. The sole reader still consumes terminal evidence; detached cleanup cannot publish operations or schedule retry.

### A08

Decision: Starting another route admission stops the drain until its result arrives. The new ordinary route ACK joins the same FIFO and cannot bypass older inputs or apply effects early. The barrier remains engaged throughout admission and draining. The head retains its queue reservation while synchronous dispatch prepares it; dequeue only after dispatch disposes the input or transfers ownership to another bounded owner, here the reserved evaluation record. Provider invocation alone is not permission to leave an unowned copy in another queue.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it.\"

QUOTE: \"Dequeue only after dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, including a reserved evaluation record when another admission starts.\"

### A09

Decision: Revoke pending semantic authority and dispose both queued commands, releasing their continuation-queue reservations. Neither may dispatch data, grant peer credit, refresh hold or start policy work. Keep the invoked unsettled provider's work reservation despite cancellation and semantic disposal. The same sole reader must continue consuming already-accepted transport packets and rejection evidence in FIFO order through the terminal record, without protocol effects. It must not be replaced by a second reader or cancelled early merely because the administrative cause has won.

QUOTE: \"Every terminal cause invalidates pending semantic authority and disposes the queued semantic backlog; none of those queued commands may later refresh hold, grant peer credit, invoke another provider or apply protocol effects.\"
QUOTE: \"Disposing continuation inputs releases their queue reservations, not reservations for already-started provider work.\"
QUOTE: \"The sole reader still drains the transport's already-accepted packets and rejection evidence in FIFO order through its one terminal record, without semantic dispatch; a second reader or early read cancellation is not the correction.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A10

Decision: The empty eligible subset does not authorize skipping invocation. Subject to the final invocation permit, runtime and deadline checks, the authorized, capacity-reserved action invokes the provider exactly once with empty route inputs. The only valid decisions list is empty. Static rejections remain separately retained for complete route preparation; they do not create policy decisions or an exemption from the route-start transition. A later revocation or elapsed bound could prevent invocation, but empty input itself cannot.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Before invocation, validate the envelope, exact next revision and canonical snapshot, then prepare the immutable policy-eligible subset and retain static rejections separately.\"
QUOTE: \"Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset.\"
QUOTE: \"The existing route-start transition has no empty-subset exemption: an authorized, capacity-reserved action invokes once with empty route inputs when no tuple is policy-eligible, and requires an empty decisions list.\"

### A11

Decision: The malformed or incomplete current result is a fault: take the existing route AdmissionFaulted terminal path, send INTERNAL_ERROR only if safe, purge routes, and neither consume the proposal's revision nor authorize an ACK. The complete valid result with an explicit policy denial is nonfatal. Subject to complete preparation and final commit guards, it atomically commits surviving routes, the POLICY rejection and the consumed revision; only then does ACK authority exist. Reserving evaluation capacity does not convert invalid decisions into an acceptable route outcome.

QUOTE: \"The inherited route-result rules distinguish malformed, incomplete or thrown results from an explicit per-route denial.\"
QUOTE: \"A current fault follows the existing route "'`AdmissionFaulted` terminal path, with `INTERNAL_ERROR` if safe, route purge and no ACK for the uncommitted proposal."
QUOTE: "An explicit denial remains nonfatal `POLICY`;"
QUOTE: "The surviving routes, rejection list and consumed revision commit atomically before ACK authority exists."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A12

Decision: Compute available RIB capacity at the final serialized commit, using then-current routing state. The initial policy preparation must not freeze a global-capacity answer. Insufficient RIB space is normal per-route CAPACITY rejection under capacity admission, not AdmissionCapacityExceeded, provider fault or whole-snapshot failure. The surviving routes, canonical rejection list and consumed revision commit atomically, after complete validation; that committed outcome authorizes an ACK. The evaluation work pool and final RIB capacity are distinct limits.

QUOTE: "insufficient final RIB capacity remains canonical per-route `CAPACITY` under capacity admission, not whole-snapshot failure or admission-work-pool refusal."
QUOTE: "The surviving routes, rejection list and consumed revision commit atomically before ACK authority exists."

Inference or gap: NONE for these decisions. The document does not specify which allowed tuples survive a capacity shortage; it refers to canonical capacity admission rather than defining that selection here.

### A13

Decision: Neither may continue as an ordinary transaction after numeric terminal replacement. The node owns the authoritative runtime gate and serialized coordinator; every live operations publication, including unrelated ones, must cross that boundary. Exhaustion closes the gate, sets host authority to Failed and invalidates outstanding admission/action permits before ordinary effects. The prepared identity plan cannot install. The queued stop completion must observe the terminal gate and cannot overwrite Failed, publish another revision or rearm an adjacency. The store supplies preflight and capture, not independent live-node terminal authority.

Document support:

QUOTE: "The node owns one authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator; the core owns pure transition/routing preparation and numeric-domain preflight."
QUOTE: "All runtime operations publications must reach this coordinator, including ones outside admission, so an unrelated counter/event/revision exhaustion revokes admission and acquisition authority too."
QUOTE: "A stop or listener-failure continuation already queued must observe the terminal gate and must not overwrite `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`, generate another revision, or rearm an adjacency."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A14

Decision: Both queries return the same frozen terminal resource values, including the two unfinished reservations recorded at T, the same terminal revision and capturedAt=T. Private later settlement/disposal cannot update those public values, create events or advance revision. The counts are last-known at terminal capture; callers cannot infer that the work remains allocated now, that cleanup has finished, or that physical resources stopped. Private disposal can release internal reservations without creating public release evidence.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Freeze its resource values, revision and `capturedAt` together; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that same terminal capture, not a new timestamp on old counts."
QUOTE: "Outstanding provider evaluations remain nonzero at that capture when unresolved; later private disposal can release internal reservations but cannot publish a new revision, event or counter."
QUOTE: "The final count is last-known at the terminal capture, not a live promise that resources remain allocated or that cleanup has finished."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A15

Decision: Disposal updates the ordinary stopped instance'"'s cleanup accounting without reopening lifecycle or event subscriptions. That canonical gauge change increments the revision once and uses a fresh capture time. The two read-only queries do not increment revision; absent another mutation, both see the disposal's resulting revision and updated gauge. Capture time remains live for ordinary stopped queries, rather than frozen as it would be after operational-domain terminal capture. A later numeric exhaustion would change that authority, but none is stated here.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Ordinary stopped instances remain queryable: later settlement may update cleanup gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions.\"
QUOTE: \"Such gauge changes are ordinary canonical transactions under the operations revision rules: increment once, with a fresh query capture time; queries themselves do not increment revisions.\"
QUOTE: \"Ordinary stopped instances retain live accounting until an operational-domain terminal barrier actually occurs.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A16

Decision: The projection is permitted for an initial capacity wait. It creates no attempt, controller token or backoff timer, and retryAttempt stays unchanged. No retryAt means no live retry timer. Disabling reconnect prevents repeat attempts, not this initial acquisition or its wait. Only identity capacity must become available for this identity-only phase; unrelated route-pool pressure does not block it. The serialized start still checks other eligibility guards, and availability is not a reservation for later provider invocation.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Initial acquisition eligible, identity pool full | Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured | "'`retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`, no `activeControllerId`; `retryAttempt` unchanged"
QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
QUOTE: "Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase; a route-capacity refusal parks that affected adjacency on route capacity as well."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A17

Decision: Backoff expiry consumes only the timer; it cannot start a new attempt while required route capacity remains unavailable. Retain/register the one waiter and ended-attempt projection, with no retryAt after the timer expires. A release notification carries no reservation: if route capacity is full again at this adjacency'"'s start check, no acquisition starts and waiting continues. Recompute blocked pools, including mandatory identity capacity. Preserve the remembered route-refusal set across these fluctuations; consume it only at actual next acquisition, or clear it on the other explicitly named satisfaction/terminal/stop transitions.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Backoff expires but capacity is still unavailable | Consume only the timer; retain/register one waiter and the ended attempt projection\"
QUOTE: \"Capacity opens and is used elsewhere before this adjacency starts | The start-turn level check keeps the waiter; an older notification carries no permit\"
QUOTE: \"Remembered refusing pools persist across capacity fluctuations and backoff until one actual next acquisition begins; they are then consumed, not inherited indefinitely.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A18

Decision: Adoption of the exact already-Established winner can reset accumulated failure history once for that success after confirming current winner/incarnation. A later success from an older losing controller is stale and cannot reset newer history. A winner still in OpenConfirm suppresses dialing and clears waiter/timer/refusing-pool scheduling state, but does not yet constitute establishment success. Cancelling its dial timer therefore preserves accumulated failures; retryable loss before establishment uses that preserved progression.

Document support:

QUOTE: \"Exact current winner enters "'`Established`, or an already-established exact winner is adopted | Confirm current winner/incarnation, apply the successful reset once for that success, and keep dial suppression; stale or duplicate success notifications cannot reset newer history"
QUOTE: "Channel adoption, identity victory and collision satisfaction before `Established` cannot perform the reset."
QUOTE: "Clearing a retry timer because a winner suppresses dialing removes its scheduling authority, not accumulated failure history."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A19

Decision: Labeling the timely identity allow as policy denial is wrong: it follows normal collision and confirmation rules, without promising that it must ultimately become established. Labeling the timely current identity deny as policy refusal is correct. Labeling local evaluation-slot exhaustion as identity policy denial is wrong: report AdmissionCapacityExceeded with the exact current admission kind/token and existing admission-fault cleanup/INTERNAL_ERROR reconnect disposition. Capacity refusal invokes no provider; it must not be represented as IDENTITY_REJECTED or a provider fault.

QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
QUOTE: "Its terminal effects follow the existing admission-fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` reconnect disposition, but do not misreport a provider fault when no provider was called."

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A20

Decision: The recommendation permits existing one-argument implementations to remain; it does not force cancellation-aware migration or separate browser/CLI interfaces. Both ports share optional process-local AdmissionEvaluationOptions as evaluate'"'s second parameter, with a required signal inside any supplied options object. AGP always supplies the options; a consumer may ignore them or explicitly adopt cancellation. Request/result DTOs and their schemas remain unchanged and credential-free. This remains a proposal requiring provider inventory, type/export review and compilation checks before adoption, not a verified compatibility result.

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A21

Decision: The provider owns its hidden descendant task'"'s cancellation and resource budget. AGP accounts for port evaluations and retained request/results, not invisible private tasks; a completed evaluation does not prove physical cleanup. The saved signal grants no authenticated-session revocation authority. It belongs only to that pending evaluation, and after the current result commits, later session events cannot reuse its cancellation authority. AGP's own evaluation reservation is releasable under settlement-plus-disposal rules, independently of the provider's hidden work.

QUOTE: \"Once a current result commits, later session events cannot reuse that evaluation's cancellation authority.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A22

Decision: Neither claim is established. The defaults are review recommendations, not measured sizing or certification for 500 simultaneous browser peers. Evaluation counts bound AGP's retained port evaluations, including revoked unsettled work and settled results awaiting disposal, in separate finite pools. Protocol/schema limits bound logical request inputs. These do not bound arbitrary provider allocations, invisible descendant work, physical JavaScript heap bytes or browser-native resource release. The design expressly provides no hundreds-of-peers endorsement for these settings.

QUOTE: \"The request's protocol/schema limits bound the retained logical input size per call; these counts do not claim to bound a provider's arbitrary allocations or physical JavaScript heap bytes.\"
QUOTE: \"No setting value here is endorsed for hundreds of peers, and no new public field or downstream migration has been applied by this draft.\"

Inference or gap: NONE.

### A23

Decision: No. Inventory every live OperationsStore publication and its prior mutations, and mediate it through prepared transactions and the common runtime-terminal gate or demonstrate it is effect-free. Two callback changes cannot close a prerequisite while independent terminalization can leave authority alive. Public work includes coordinated event types/closed schemas/FSM and operations documentation, capacity settings and effective defaults, gauge catalog meanings, timer/queue projections, retry projection reasons, terminal capture semantics, and the close-setting interval migration. If adopting cancellation options, complete type/export, provider inventory and compatibility checks. Gauge names alone establish none of these contracts.

QUOTE: \"Before implementation can close this prerequisite, inventory every live runtime OperationsStore publication and each associated pre-publication mutation; route them through the same prepared-transaction/terminal gate or demonstrate they are effect-free.\"
QUOTE: \"Both additions require coordinated core FSM, closed session-event schema/type and operations documentation changes.\"

### A24

Decision: Identity success does not remove the outer OPEN bound. It remains active through OpenConfirm even when negotiated hold is zero. Once elapsed, its existing OpenExpired authority must end the opening attempt, subject to the runtime gate and existing terminal ownership, rather than permitting unlimited confirmation wait. Normal successful establishment ends the bound; teardown also cancels it. The completed identity evaluation supplies no continuing cancellation or result authority over this later phase.

QUOTE: \"Preserve the outer opening deadline through "'`OpenConfirm`, including when negotiated hold is zero"
QUOTE: "after identity commit, the still-active OPEN timer retains its separate authority through confirmation."
QUOTE: "The OPEN timer remains armed until `Established` or teardown; admission success cannot leave an unlimited confirmation phase when hold is zero."

Inference or gap: NONE for the bound and its end conditions. The full existing OpenExpired action list is referenced rather than reproduced in this document.

Those details cannot be reconstructed from this document alone. This does not prevent the decisions above, but it limits implementation completeness from a single supplied source.
